speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings; to better understand what is happening, could you tell me exactly when this pain started and if it is triggered by touching or pressing on the ear?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporomandibular Joint (TMJ) dysfunction causing referred otalgia and mechanical irritation of the post-tympanoplasty ear canal.

The patient's shooting pain while eating suggests jaw joint involvement, which can refer pain to the ear and cause muscle tension that irritates the healing ear canal. Given the history of stress and poor sleep, I recommend a trial of jaw rest and analgesics.
